mode: AR (DSpark off), INT8 weights, FP8 KV in HBM

ucie_hop_s.note: One neighbour traversal, hardware floor, no software: UCIe PHY plus die-to-die adapter under 2 ns, on-die routing from the compute tile to the die edge ~1.5 ns (15 mm of repeated wire at ~0.1 ns/mm), and flit synchronisation into the receiver's clock and buffering of about five 1 GHz cycles. Stated 10 ns; the range spans a lean PHY-only path to a buffered one.
ucie_hop_s.source: UCIe latency 'sub-nanosecond to 2 ns' (https://semiengineering.com/what-is-ucie/ ; https://awavesemi.com/the-ucie-chiplet-interconnect-standard/); decomposition in docs/ANALYTICAL_REPORT.md

technology.board_link_LAT_source: tools/qwen_rom_rt_token_stream4_w12.py --coll-lat 339 (the measured TP4 token's collective LAT)

measured_attention.note: KV_IDEAL L0 5,283 = chained 5,282: attention is engine-bound, the KV fill (1,311 cycles at 96% of 4.0 TB/s) is hidden by prefetch

engine_tiling.finding: at G 6,144 TP8 halves every stream (qkv 64->32, o 48->24, gu 256->128, down 144->72, head 1,584->800) at the same utilisation; ROM depth 20,016 -> 10,016 words (5 -> 3 code banks). A half-size TP8 die (G 3,072) keeps the TP4 stream times exactly, so it only adds communication

scaling_rules.me_ops: window - TP4 stream + TP8 stream; priced adders (relays 95, MUL_LAT, band +7) kept per op (conservative: a shorter TP8 die has fewer relay stations)
scaling_rules.attention: TP8-A: stream 1024 -> 512 (4 MiB -> 2 MiB a die over 128 PC landings), fixed 131.0 kept (central); best halves the fixed part too, worst keeps the full fixed part plus no halving of its tail; TP8-B/H: unchanged (half the landings/engines)
scaling_rules.su: rmsnorm/residual/attn_tail replicated (unchanged); qknorm_rope and softmax_norm scale with heads a die: 0.5 central/best, 1.0 worst
scaling_rules.allreduce: +20 cycles (fold 2 + 7 x 5 vs 2 + 3 x 5); board LAT 339 per crossing unchanged on a K4 4-package board; serialisation 256 words unchanged (one word a cycle to all destinations)
scaling_rules.head: lm_head stream 1,584 -> 800, + 10 cycles for the 8-way argmax gather
scaling_rules.l0: TP8-A: cold KV fill halves (the 222-cycle KV constants kept); B/H unchanged

system_die.partition: row engines (near-HBM attention) move with the HBM PHYs, controllers, CDC and landing frames: only q (<= 1,280 values) and the attention result cross UCIe, twice a layer; the 4 MiB KV stream never crosses

kv_landing_only_alternative.note: move only PHY/controller/landing, keep row engines: 4 MiB a layer a die crosses UCIe-A at 4.2 TB/s
kv_landing_only_alternative.verdict: worse: same latency, ~0.6 mJ/token/die more, 7 mm more UCIe shoreline

system_die.packaging: per package: 2 ROM dies + 2 system dies (or 4 half-size, one per stack pair) + 8 stacks; the stacks move from the ROM-die E/W edges to the system dies, so the interposer grows to ~3.5-4 reticles (B200 is ~3.3): roadmap CoWoS-L class, not B200-identical

Option 1a: system die, collective IO stays on the ROM die
side_by_side.grade: modelled crossings on the priced TP4 token

problems_tp8.divisibility: none: 32 Q / 8 KV heads -> 4 Q + 1 KV per die (GQA groups whole); FFN 12,288/8 = 1,536; vocab 151,936/8 = 18,992; the engine tiling keeps lane utilisation (qkv/gu 1.0, o/down 0.889, head 0.989 vs 0.999) at G 6,144 -- the matvec stream halves, no lanes idle
problems_tp8.tp8_is_the_kv_limit: TP8 is the largest legal split: 1 KV head a die; TP16 would replicate KV heads
problems_tp8.compute_halves_only_on_stream: the measured ME windows are mostly fixed latency (x broadcast, tree, relays 95/op, band +7): halving the weight stream saves only 256 cycles a layer (512 -> 256 stream); the big compute saving is attention (KV per die halves) and only if each die keeps 4 stacks and 24 row engines
problems_tp8.collective_does_not_shrink: the all-reduce payload is the full hidden vector (4,096 FP32) on every die at any TP; the one-shot fold grows 17 -> 37 cycles; the board crossing LAT 339 is unchanged only on a fully connected 4-package board (K4)
problems_tp8.collective_share: link share of the token rises from 34.6% (TP4) to 42.3% (TP8-A) / 38.3% (TP8-B)
problems_tp8.board_topology: 4 packages must be fully connected (3 board neighbours each); on a 2x2 board mesh the diagonal pair is relayed (+343 cycles an all-reduce) and TP8-A falls to +5.6%
problems_tp8.serdes: off-package destinations per die 2 -> 6: per-package egress 307 -> 922 GB/s (77% of the 1.19 TB/s 90-lane 2-die-package SerDes budget, 307 of 397 GB/s per K4 neighbour), all with RS(544,514) FEC; 3x SerDes lanes per die
problems_tp8.unclosed_path: the TP4 collective path (qfd_io_collective TT -341, qfd_io_xfifo TT -772, qfd_link_rx128 TT -696) is not closed today; TP8 widens it (7 receive FIFOs, 8-input fold)
problems_tp8.critical_path_imbalance: none: every die runs the same schedule in lockstep (identical geometry per die)

closure_risk.TP4: r21b at 882.8 mm2 known, 24.8 mm2 over the reticle; tile, spine and collective not closed
closure_risk.TP8: die ~802 mm2 (6.5% margin, 9.2% at linear ROM); tiles lose 2 of 5 code banks (shorter tile, smaller ROM fanout: plausibly easier, unproven); collective path widened to N 8 (7 receive FIFOs, 8-input fold) on a path already failing TT; 3x SerDes; 8 ROM images; K4 board
closure_risk.SYS: ROM die ~795.5 mm2 (7.3% margin; 787.9 mm2, 8.2%, with the collective IO moved) with the same tile/spine/collective closure as today; a new system die (HBM PHY/ctrl/row engines/host/PLL, small, edge-bound) and two UCIe interfaces; larger interposer

decision.rule: owner: adopt TP8 if it gives better total decode throughput and per-user rate after all communication overhead, without compute/communication problems; otherwise adopt the companion system die (option 1)
decision.compute_problems: none found (heads, FFN and vocab divide by 8; lane utilisation unchanged; lockstep dies)
decision.communication_problems: none blocking: the all-reduce grows only +20 cycles (+40 a layer, +0.7% of the token) and fits the SerDes budget at 77%; it does not shrink, so its share rises 34.6% -> 42.3%. Two hard requirements: a fully connected 4-package board (K4) and 3x off-package SerDes lanes a die
decision.verdict: ADOPT TP8 (variant A: 8 dies, 4 HBM stacks a die, 4 B200-class 2-die packages, K4 board)
why: per user 6,586.9 vs 5,492.7 tok/s (+19.9% central; range 6,127.9-6,673.2, worst case still +11.6%) after the larger collective
aggregate per instance 32,160 vs 25,362 tok/s (modelled ceiling)

the die drops to ~802 mm2 (6.5% reticle margin; 9.2% if ROM area scales linearly) from 882.8 mm2 (-2.9%), with the same tile count and shorter tiles; option 1 regains a similar margin (7.3%) but loses 0.5-1.4% per user and needs a new die and a larger interposer
TP8-A uses the existing package class (2 dies + 8 stacks, B200-type); option 1 does not
conditions: the 4 packages must be fully connected on the board; on a 2x2 board mesh TP8-A falls to +5.6% and TP8-B to -3.2%

each die keeps 4 stacks and the 24 near-HBM row engines: with 2 stacks a die (TP8-B, 16 stacks) per-user gain is +8.7% and the KV-bound aggregate is unchanged (+0.3%), which does not meet the 'better total throughput' leg
the attention halving (1 KV head spread over all 128 PC landings) is modelled, not measured: a TP8 L1 at P8191 on the STREAM4 vehicle (KV_NH=1) is the confirming run
costs_flagged: 2x logic dies (8 vs 4) and 2x HBM stacks (32 vs 16) per instance: aggregate per die -37%, per logic mm2 -30%, per total silicon (stacks at 1,150 mm2) -36%; the iso-area Qwen headline against GPUs gets worse
collective share of the token 34.6% -> 42.3%; the TP4 collective path is still not closed and TP8 widens it (7 receive FIFOs, 8-input fold)
3x SerDes lanes a die with RS FEC: always-on lane power (~0.73 W a lane) unpriced
decision.alternative: if the owner weighs per-die / iso-silicon efficiency over per-instance speed, option 1a (system die, collective stays on the ROM die) keeps per-die throughput and loses 0.5% per user

unvalidated: every TP8 and system-die number is modelled from measured TP4 windows; no TP8 or system-die RTL was run
the r21c embedding fetch (+248 typical / +567 worst a token) is uncharged in every option, as in the 218,472 basis
the TP4 aggregate is a modelled ceiling (KV stream at 96% of 4.0 TB/s a die vs tile windows); no batched run exists
SerDes always-on lane power (0.73 W a lane) for 3x lanes is not in any rate
system-die host/PLL/CSR 12 mm2 and UCIe module 5 mm2 are modelled
